items_missed: Set the Agenda: never checked whether the 8/17 move date on file still worked, gave no real agenda statement (what he'd cover / how long it takes), and never got an explicit 'sound good?' confirmation before diving in.

Probe: didn't ask about stairs/floors at either address, special considerations (narrow hallways, tight turns), packing needs, box count, storage stops, or access concerns (elevator/parking/HOA) -- all punted to the walkthrough with no quick gut-check taken now.
Walkthrough booking: never asked 'any other questions before I let you go,' and only covered branch hours/how to reach them loosely ('call us if anything changes') rather than stating it directly.
Politeness: used the customer's name only twice across the whole call ('Pam' once at the open, 'Ron' once at the close) -- short of the 3+ threshold.
Bonus: no rapport-building moment (no laugh, no personal connection) -- stayed transactional throughout, even during the mid-call hiccup where she needed to loop in her husband.
top_strength: Grant absorbed a mid-call curveball -- the customer stopped mid-quote-recap to say she hadn't run this by her husband yet and handed him the phone -- without losing his place, then gave a genuinely clear, reassuring walkthrough of what the virtual walkthrough actually involves ('you'll show me everything we're going to be moving for you and then I'll be able to get you an estimate after that'), which visibly landed: the customer replied 'Much better than me just trying to think it through this off.'
coaching_note: You skipped the agenda opener entirely and went straight into reading back the quote form -- a quick 'I'll grab a few details and get you set up, should take about 10 minutes, sound good?' up front sets the pace and gets a small early yes. Once you clocked this was a 3,100 sq ft home headed to a walkthrough, you still had time to ask one or two quick questions (stairs, packing needs) so the walkthrough itself moves faster -- right now those get punted completely. Also watch the name mix-up: you booked the appointment under 'Ron' and closed with 'talk to you tomorrow, Ron' after opening the call with 'Pam' -- worth a quick double-check on who's actually primary before you hang up so the confirmation email doesn't go out with the wrong name.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient through an awkward mid-call handoff, but transitions leaned on repeated fillers ('gotcha,' 'alrighty') with no empathy statement acknowledging the customer's moment of hesitation.
